That 2.2% spread is on the same code. Its 6-step-shorter recipe now times the same as E049. My mechanism: max-autotune (Triton and cuDNN candidate choice) plus cudagraph pool placement picks different kernels on each build. That moves wall time by about ±1–1.5% (1 SD ≈ 0.04–0.06 s), and the shift is correlated across all 3 trials. Consequences:
   - Every time 'keep' decided by less than ~2% since E036 is partly a draw on the build. This includes E049 over E046, and my misses on E050, E056 and E059.
   - Time levers below ~2% (whitening detach, BN tweaks) cannot be judged from ar.py wall time. They need per-step CUDA-event timing, or several builds.
   - Corollary nobody has proposed: the reported score is one build's draw. A recipe with fewer distinct compiled graphs (fewer resolution × freeze variants) should show less build variance, and possibly better mean kernels, because autotune is less likely to land on a bad choice.

2. Accuracy noise. Per-seed SD is ~0.25 pp, so the 3-seed SD is ~0.15 pp. E059 (E046 rebuilt) read 0.7543 on seeds 0–2 against its earlier 0.7540, so the build component of accuracy looks small (≤0.06 pp). The +0.25 epoch top-up in E049 has no measurable accuracy value at this power. The seeds 0–2 ≥0.753 gate remains the binding constraint. A recipe with population mean ~0.7535 passes about 50% of the time.

3. Where time goes per step:
   - Resolution-independent work weighs most at 20–24 px: three Muon NS graphs, fused SGD and Lookahead.
   - Freezes save more than their FLOP share because they also drop BN/GELU backward and a Muon call (E028, E046).
   - E056 (ReLU) cut time by 4.7%, which suggests activation bytes matter. Part of that may be a lucky build, per point 1.

4. Muon renormalizes filters and fixes the update norm. Filter ||ΔW||/||W|| therefore just tracks the LR schedule, so I094's filter curves are tautological. Freeze cost scales with the LR integral removed while downstream layers still adapt (E037 −0.4, E055 −0.15, E053 ~−0.2 on biased seeds). It is not a threshold.

5. Steps carry accuracy; early pixels do not (E026 and E033 were free, E041 and E031 cost). The end-game is at a local optimum: E025, E030, E032 and E044 all hurt.

6. Settled by reading the code:
   - BN scale is already frozen, so I092 is a no-op.
   - Only fine labels are supplied, so H1.8 is blocked.
   - Filter wd is inert.

7. Best paths:
   - Identical-math systems work: batch all Muon NS work into one graph, and skip NS for groups whose LR is ~0.
   - ReLU plus a small top-up.
   - Fewer compiled variants, to cut build-time variance.
   - Always evaluate on several builds, or with CUDA events.

8. PCIe judge: expect times 5–10% higher.

W5 (contrarian), after E059. The tip is E049: 5.198 s, seeds 0–2 at 0.7535. Rebuilds of E049 read 5.21–5.22 s, with seeds 0–2 at 0.7552 and 0.7536.

1. Time noise between builds is larger than anyone has priced, me included. E046 (commit 8a2452a, 231 steps) measured 5.079 s originally and 5.193 s when rebuilt in E059. That 2.2% spread is on the same code. Its 6-step-shorter recipe now times the same as E049. My mechanism: max-autotune (Triton and cuDNN candidate choice) plus cudagraph pool placement picks different kernels on each build. That moves wall time by about ±1–1.5% (1 SD ≈ 0.04–0.06 s), and the shift is correlated across all 3 trials. Consequences:
   - Every time 'keep' decided by less than ~2% since E036 is partly a draw on the build. This includes E049 over E046, and my misses on E050, E056 and E059.
   - Time levers below ~2% (whitening detach, BN tweaks) cannot be judged from ar.py wall time. They need per-step CUDA-event timing, or several builds.
   - Corollary nobody has proposed: the reported score is one build's draw. A recipe with fewer distinct compiled graphs (fewer resolution × freeze variants) should show less build variance, and possibly better mean kernels, because autotune is less likely to land on a bad choice.

2. Accuracy noise. Per-seed SD is ~0.25 pp, so the 3-seed SD is ~0.15 pp. E059 (E046 rebuilt) read 0.7543 on seeds 0–2 against its earlier 0.7540, so the build component of accuracy looks small (≤0.06 pp). The +0.25 epoch top-up in E049 has no measurable accuracy value at this power. The seeds 0–2 ≥0.753 gate remains the binding constraint. A recipe with population mean ~0.7535 passes about 50% of the time.

3. Where time goes per step:
   - Resolution-independent work weighs most at 20–24 px: three Muon NS graphs, fused SGD and Lookahead.
   - Freezes save more than their FLOP share because they also drop BN/GELU backward and a Muon call (E028, E046).
   - E056 (ReLU) cut time by 4.7%, which suggests activation bytes matter. Part of that may be a lucky build, per point 1.

4. Muon renormalizes filters and fixes the update norm. Filter ||ΔW||/||W|| therefore just tracks the LR schedule, so I094's filter curves are tautological. Freeze cost scales with the LR integral removed while downstream layers still adapt (E037 −0.4, E055 −0.15, E053 ~−0.2 on biased seeds). It is not a threshold.

5. Steps carry accuracy; early pixels do not (E026 and E033 were free, E041 and E031 cost). The end-game is at a local optimum: E025, E030, E032 and E044 all hurt.

6. Settled by reading the code:
   - BN scale is already frozen, so I092 is a no-op.
   - Only fine labels are supplied, so H1.8 is blocked.
   - Filter wd is inert.

7. Best paths:
   - Identical-math systems work: batch all Muon NS work into one graph, and skip NS for groups whose LR is ~0.
   - ReLU plus a small top-up.
   - Fewer compiled variants, to cut build-time variance.
   - Always evaluate on several builds, or with CUDA events.

8. PCIe judge: expect times 5–10% higher.

Unsure about:
- the size of the build component in the 20-seed accuracy mean;
- whether E056's time gain survives a rebuild.

forecasts.reason: TrainingData has no coarse labels, so the gate blocks the run; anything measured is a tip rebuild.
BN weight already has requires_grad=False, so this is a no-op and any reading is rebuild noise.
The expected saving (~0.5%) is below the ~2% build-time spread, and fixing the 64x-LR bias early probably costs ~0.05–0.1 pp.
Muon's fixed-norm updates make the filter ΔW/W curves follow the LR schedule, so they cannot separate E028 from E037 beyond what the schedule already says.

cruxes: What is the build-to-build SD of ar.py wall time for the same commit (E046 read 5.08 and then 5.19)? Does it shrink when the recipe compiles fewer graph variants? If the SD is ≥1%, every sub-2% time keep since E036 is unproven.
Does E056's ReLU time saving (−4.7%) survive a fresh rebuild, measured with per-step CUDA-event timing?

How much of the per-step time at 20/24 px is resolution-independent Muon NS, SGD and Lookahead work (three separate NS graphs)? Would batching them into one graph give an identical-math saving of ≥3%?
